:::{#exm-fisher-kl-poisson}
#### Curvature of the divergence for Poisson data

Differentiating the divergence of @exm-model-kl-poisson twice with respect to $\rate$ gives
$\deriv{\rate} \kldivf{\rate_0}{\rate} = 1 - \rate_0 / \rate$
and $\dderiv{\rate} \kldivf{\rate_0}{\rate} = \rate_0 / \rate^2$,
so at $\rate = \rate_0$ the second derivative is $1/\rate_0$,
which is the expected information of one observation (@exm-information-poisson).
A numerical second difference of the divergence,
summed directly over the Poisson probabilities, agrees:

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
rate_true <- 3
kl_div <- function(rate) {
  x <- 0:200
  log_ratio <- dpois(x, rate_true, log = TRUE) - dpois(x, rate, log = TRUE)
  sum(dpois(x, rate_true) * log_ratio)
}
h <- 1e-3
kl_values <- c(
  kl_div(rate_true - h),
  kl_div(rate_true),
  kl_div(rate_true + h)
)
c(
  second_difference = sum(kl_values * c(1, -2, 1)) / h^2,
  expected_information = 1 / rate_true
)
```

:::
